articles.dek: During Frieze week, blocks of ice holding effigies of famous artists appeared outside the fair and London's auction houses. What does the work say about value, and what is left once the ice has gone?
articles.credit: Image: ANTI-FRIEZE, London, October 2025. Courtesy Konn Artiss
articles.body:
Frieze week is when London's art market is at its most confident: the fair, the auctions and the gallery openings all pulling in the same direction. In October 2025, Konn Artiss chose that week to put the market on ice.

The work

Outside Frieze London stood five large blocks of ice, each holding an effigy of an artist whose name is now a brand: Damien Hirst, Andy Warhol, Tracey Emin, Jeff Koons and KAWS.[ap-antifrieze] Elsewhere in the city, further blocks appeared outside major galleries and auction houses, including one beside a framed image at Phillips.[tan-frieze]

What it says

The joke lands quickly. These are artists whose work is collected, stored, insured and preserved as carefully as any asset, and here they are frozen solid, in public, with no one to keep them cold. The longer argument takes the whole week to make. As the ice melts, what is left is water, debris and a crowd of people who stopped to watch. Value, the work suggests, is a kind of attention, and attention melts too.

Does it work?

As a piece of timing and staging, yes. It is legible in seconds, photographs well and makes a clear point in a place where that point is hardest to ignore. The weaker side is that critique of the art market made during Frieze week is itself very good publicity, and the project benefits from the attention it mocks. That tension is probably deliberate. It is also worth noticing.

VerdictA sharp, well-timed intervention that is better at asking its question than answering it. Worth knowing as a marker of how contemporary artists are using spectacle to talk back to the market.

articles.title: The Washington Ghost: satire as a printed newspaper
articles.dek: Ten thousand copies, handed out in Venice. Is a newspaper an artwork?
articles.credit: Image: The Washington Ghost, Venice, 2025. [Image to supply]
articles.body:
Before Jeff Bezos's wedding in Venice in June 2025, more than 10,000 copies of a satirical newspaper called The Washington Ghost were distributed in the city, credited to Konn Artiss.[gb-venice]

A newspaper as a medium

The form is the cleverest part. A newspaper looks like information, costs nothing and is designed to be thrown away. Putting satire into that format lets the work move through a city the way news does, hand to hand, without a gallery or a ticket. It also borrows the name and look of a famous newspaper owned by the very person it mocks, which sharpens the joke.

What survives

Most copies will have been binned within a day. The ones that remain become something else: a document of an event, and possibly a collectable. That shift, from free giveaway to object with value, is exactly the process the artist's later work at Frieze makes fun of.

Note on sourcesFAD Magazine reports that related work was displayed at the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.[fad-ghost] We have not confirmed this independently.

articles.title: Zara Muse and Konn Artiss: two ways to talk about value
articles.dek: One builds it into the paint. The other lets it melt on the pavement.
articles.body:
Put side by side, these two artists could hardly look more different. Zara Muse makes solid, textured portraits meant to hang on a wall for decades. Konn Artiss makes interventions that are designed to vanish within days. Yet both are, in their own way, talking about value.

Permanence and its opposite

Muse's paintings are about building up: layer after layer of paint, a career built from a personal turning point, portraits of women chosen for their strength.[ap-muse] Artiss's work is about things falling apart: frozen effigies of famous artists left to melt, newspapers made to be thrown away.[ap-antifrieze]

What each asks of you

A Muse painting asks you to slow down and look closely at a surface. An Artiss intervention asks you to notice the system around the art: who is famous, who is paid, who controls the street. Reading them together is a useful reminder that contemporary art covers both: the made object and the questions about why objects are valued at all.

guides.title: Van Gogh, All Our Paintings
guides.html:
The Kröller-Müller Museum is showing all 88 of its paintings by Vincent van Gogh together, for the first time since 1984.[kmm-vangogh-all] The rooms are grouped by three ideas central to his life and work, faith, hope and love, and the museum points back to a sermon he gave in 1876.[kmm-vangogh-all]

Things to look for: The Potato Eaters and The Old Tower at Nuenen from his years in the Netherlands; Terrace of a Café at Night (Place du Forum), Portrait of Joseph Roulin and L'Arlésienne (Madame Ginoux); The Good Samaritan (after Delacroix); and Sorrowing Old Man ('At Eternity's Gate').[kmm-vangogh-all] Bridge at Arles (Pont de Langlois) has a display you can touch, with audio description.[kmm-vangogh-all]

You need a museum and park ticket plus a timed exhibition ticket, which costs nothing extra and is booked online. The museum opens Tuesday to Sunday and on public holidays, 10.00 to 17.00, and is closed on 1 January.[kmm-vangogh-all] Our suggestion is to allow two hours, and more if you want to walk in the park.

guides.title: Andy Warhol. Line and image
guides.html:
This exhibition looks at Andy Warhol as a draughtsman. It shows about 150 drawings alongside paintings, screenprints on paper, photographs and archive papers, from an early Self-Portrait (1942) to acrylic drawings linked to The Last Supper (1986).[lux-warhol-ligne] It is curated by the art historian Alain Cueff and organised by GrandPalaisRmn.[lux-warhol-ligne]

The show is in five parts: his early work as an advertising illustrator, handwriting, faces and masks, gay imagery that he long kept private, and death, which became a lasting concern after he was shot in 1968.[lux-warhol-ligne] Things to look for: The Nation's Nightmare (1951), Feet (about 1959), and the methods he used to make a line, such as stamping, blotted or transferred lines, stencils and collage.[lux-warhol-ligne]

The museum opens daily from 10.30 to 19.00, until 22.00 on Mondays, and is closed on 25 December. A full ticket costs 14 euros, and entry is free for under 16s.[lux-warhol-ligne] Our suggestion is to allow about an hour and a half.

guides.title: The Light Spreads Out, and Glittering Things Start Appearing All Around Me
guides.html:
This show at the Yayoi Kusama Museum in Shinjuku looks at Kusama's work through the idea of light.[kusama-museum-light] It runs from early drawings of the 1950s and the collages made after she returned to Japan, through the Infinity Nets and paintings from the 1980s onwards, to the recent My Eternal Soul series.[kusama-museum-light] Mirror rooms, prints and sculptures that use glitter are also on show.[kusama-museum-light]

Things to look for: the early A Flower #6 (1953) set against later paintings such as Longing for Infinite Heaven (2020); a large sculpture covered in mosaic tiles with metal leaf; and an outdoor ladder sculpture with mirrors, shown in Japan for the first time.[kusama-museum-light]

Tickets are sold only in advance on the museum's website, each for a 90 minute slot, and the museum is open Thursday to Sunday and on national holidays.[kusama-museum-light] It is closed from 28 December 2026 to 6 January 2027.[kusama-museum-light] Our suggestion is to plan on using the full 90 minutes.

guides.title: Basquiat, the Blue Ribbon Paintings, and the Art of Reproduction
guides.venue: Princeton University Art Museum, Princeton, New Jersey
guides.html:
The centre of this exhibition is a group of eleven paintings Jean-Michel Basquiat made in 1984, known as the Blue Ribbon paintings.[princeton-basquiat] Around them the museum has gathered nearly all of Basquiat's known print projects, with work connected to Robert Rauschenberg and to the printmaker Bob Blackburn.[princeton-basquiat]

Things to look for: how the eleven paintings relate to one another as a set, including Blue Ribbon II (1984); and how the prints carry Basquiat's images into another medium, which is the subject the title points to.[princeton-basquiat]

Special exhibition tours are listed for 28 November and 5 December 2026.[princeton-basquiat] After Princeton the show travels to the High Museum of Art (19 February to 16 May 2027) and the Frist Art Museum (4 June to 29 August 2027).[princeton-basquiat] Our suggestion is to allow about an hour.

guides.title: Kandinsky
guides.html:
This exhibition at Palazzo Bonaparte on Piazza Venezia shows some sixty works by Wassily Kandinsky, organised by the Centre Pompidou in Paris with Arthemisia.[pompidou-kandinsky-rome] It follows his whole career: early figurative painting, the first steps into abstraction in Munich, his return to Russia during the revolutionary years, his teaching at the Bauhaus and his last years in Paris.[pompidou-kandinsky-rome]

Things to look for: Le Parc de Saint-Cloud, allée ombragée (1906), a landscape from before abstraction; Bild mit rotem Fleck (Painting with Red Spot, 1914); Gelb-Rot-Blau (Yellow-Red-Blue, 1925) and Dunkle Kühle (1927) from the Bauhaus years; and Bleu de ciel (1940) and Cercle et Carré (1943) from Paris.[pompidou-kandinsky-rome] Seeing the 1906 and 1943 works in one visit shows how far his painting travelled.

The exhibition opens from 9.00 to 19.30 Monday to Thursday and from 9.00 to 21.00 Friday to Sunday.[pompidou-kandinsky-rome] Our suggestion is to allow an hour to an hour and a half.

guides.title: Beatriz Milhazes: gravuras do acervo da Pinacoteca de São Paulo
guides.venue: Pinacoteca de São Paulo, São Paulo
guides.html:
This exhibition brings together 27 prints by Beatriz Milhazes, made between 1996 and 2019 and shown as a set for the first time, according to Pace, one of her galleries.[pace-milhazes-pina] The prints come from her long collaboration with Durham Press, a print studio in the United States.[pace-milhazes-pina][whitecube-milhazes-pina] White Cube, which also represents her, reports that Milhazes gave the whole selection to the Pinacoteca's collection, and names the curator as Renato Menezes.[whitecube-milhazes-pina]

Things to look for: O pato (1996) beside Noite de verão (2006), which show how her arrangement of shapes, colour and empty space changed over ten years; and motifs drawn from chita fabric, embroidery and weaving, such as discs, mandalas, bead necklaces and flowers.[pace-milhazes-pina]

We could not read the Pinacoteca's own page, so check opening hours and tickets there before you go. Our suggestion is to allow about an hour for the prints, and longer if you plan to see the rest of the museum.

guides.title: Picasso: Back to the Origins
guides.html:
This exhibition, which opens in February, looks at how Pablo Picasso's early life shaped his work. It shows lithographs, etchings, manuscripts and ceramics.[naples-picasso-origins] The museum traces his youth and training in Galicia and in Barcelona, then his move to the south of France after the Second World War, when he reconnected with the Mediterranean.[naples-picasso-origins] The museum also links the work to unsettled family life and personal loss in his early years, and to how he drew on his cultural roots.[naples-picasso-origins]

Things to look for: how the same artist works across prints, ceramics and handwritten papers, and how themes from his youth come back in work made decades later.[naples-picasso-origins]

When we checked, the museum's page said tickets were coming soon and did not give the number of works, the lenders or the gallery. Check the page for opening hours before you go.[naples-picasso-origins] Our suggestion is to allow about an hour.

guides.title: Basquiat: Figures, Signs, Symbols
guides.html:
This is a small, focused show: ten works by Jean-Michel Basquiat, all lent by the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection.[pamm-basquiat] The museum describes it as the largest presentation of Basquiat's work in Florida to date.[pamm-basquiat] It was organised by Franklin Sirmans, director of PAMM, and Megan Kincaid, curator of the Griffin Collection, and an illustrated publication goes with it.[pamm-basquiat]

Things to look for: with only ten paintings, there is room to stand with each one and read the figures, signs and symbols the title names. It is also worth comparing how those three elements share space from one canvas to the next.

Check opening days before you go: the museum lists itself as open Monday and Friday to Sunday, 11am to 6pm, and closed Tuesday to Thursday.[pamm-basquiat] The show runs until 6 June 2027.[pamm-basquiat] Our suggestion is to allow 45 minutes to an hour.
